newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices flat to down 1/4.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices flat to down 1/4.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices closed flat to down 1/4 point while primary market deals were priced to sell.

One trader cited "a fair amount" of bid wanted lists in circulation. The lists, which totaled roughly $250 million, contained "a lot of stuff that nobody wants," the trader said. He judged muni cash prices down 1/4 to 3/8.
"It just seems to be very heavy. A lot of lack of interest is really what's going on," the trader said.
"The new issues that are coming are pretty cheap because nobody wants to underwrite bonds and lug them around for two weeks at this point. They'll probably be dying to have them in January."
While a second trader judged the market down 1/4 point, a municipal analyst said the overall market ended unchanged after having been up about 1/4 point. Activity was moderate, the analyst said.
Dollar bonds ended unchanged to up slightly, he said. High-grades ended unchanged overall, but better by two basis points in spots, the analyst said.

In debt futures, the March municipal contract closed down 6/32 at 114-30/32. The March T-bond contract closed down 15/32 at 112-2/32. The MOB spread was 92 ticks. In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond closed down 16/32 at 97-12/32 to yield 6.70.
In new issues, Smith Barney Inc repriced $222 million Indiana Health Facility Financing Authority hospital revenue bonds at a top yield of 6.039 percent in 2021.
Bear Stearns & Co repriced $159.5 million New York State Dormitory Authority bond offering, lowering the top yield in 2021 to approximately 6.128 percent from 6.15 percent.
Smith Barney also repriced Washington's $81.2 million general obligation bond isues, lowering yields in the 2015 and 2017 maturities. The 2019 maturity had a 5.875 percent yield to maturity.

Thursday's negotiated and competitive sales are expected to total $207 million in 14 issues. Ten competitive sales totaling $76 million are scheduled, the largest being a $17 million New Rochelle School District, N.Y., deal.

Four negotiated deals are scheduled totaling $130.9 million. Topping the list is a $75 million Alabama Industrial Development Authority deal via JP Morgan Securities Inc. The deal is subject to the alternative minimum tax.
